title: Actor Vijay's TVK Wins Tamil Nadu, Ending 59 Years of Dravidian Party Dominance
detail: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), the political party founded by film actor Vijay, emerged as the single largest party in its first-ever state assembly election in Tamil Nadu. The result breaks a 59-year streak of dominance by the two established Dravidian parties — the DMK and AIADMK — that have governed Tamil Nadu since 1967. TVK ran on a platform of new-generation governance, anti-corruption, and Tamil cultural identity beyond the Dravidian legacy. The result sent shockwaves through India's regional party landscape and was seen as a sign of voter appetite for new political alternatives beyond established dynasties.

media.caption: Vijay's TVK wins Tamil Nadu elections, breaking decades of Dravidian party dominance

title: Cabinet Approves Two New Semiconductor Manufacturing Units Worth ₹3,936 Crore
detail: The Union Cabinet approved two semiconductor manufacturing projects under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), with cumulative investment of approximately ₹3,936 crore (~$470 million). Crystal Matrix Limited will establish India's first commercial Mini/Micro-LED display facility using Gallium Nitride (GaN) technology at Dholera, Gujarat. Suchi Semicon Private Limited will set up an Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility in Surat capable of producing over 1,033 million discrete semiconductor chips annually. The two projects are expected to create 2,230 skilled jobs. Total approved projects under ISM reached 12, with cumulative investments of ₹1.64 lakh crore (~$19.7 billion), reflecting India's strategic push to reduce chip import dependency.

sources.name: Prime Minister's Office, Government of India

media.caption: Cabinet approves new semiconductor manufacturing units in Gujarat under India Semiconductor Mission
